questions.title: F-string Birthday Card
questions.description:
A community radio station prints a birthday greeting card for its listeners.
Read the listener's name and age, then build the greeting line with an f-string.

Input Format:
Line 1: the listener's name (letters and spaces)
Line 2: the listener's age, an integer

Output Format:
Print exactly: Hello <name>, you are <age> years old.

Constraints:
1 <= len(name) <= 50, 1 <= age <= 120
questions.sampleoutput1: Hello Ada, you are 36 years old.
questions.sampleoutput2: Hello Grace Hopper, you are 85 years old.
questions.output1: Hello Linus, you are 25 years old.
questions.output2: Hello Margaret, you are 40 years old.
questions.output3: Hello Raj, you are 12 years old.
questions.sourcecode:
name = input()
age = int(input())
print(f"Hello {name}, you are {age} years old.")

questions.title: Price Tag Two Decimals
questions.description:
A shop's price tag printer always shows money with exactly two decimal places.
Read one price value and print it formatted to exactly 2 decimals with an f-string.

Input Format:
One line: the price (a number, possibly with decimals)

Output Format:
The price printed with exactly two decimal places.

Constraints:
0 <= price <= 100000
questions.sourcecode:
price = float(input())
print(f"{price:.2f}")

questions.title: Case Shift Trio Drill
questions.description:
A text-tooling lab asks you to demonstrate the three classic case methods on one word.
Read a word and print its uppercase, lowercase and swapcase forms, one per line.

Input Format:
One line: a single word (letters and digits only)

Output Format:
Three lines: upper, lower, swapcase - in that order.

Constraints:
1 <= len(word) <= 60, letters and digits only
questions.sampleoutput2:
HELLO WORLD
hello world
hEllO wORLD
questions.sourcecode:
word = input()
print(word.upper())
print(word.lower())
print(word.swapcase())

questions.title: Comma Tag Splitter
questions.description:
An article editor stores topic tags in one comma-separated string.
Split the string on commas and print each tag on its own line.

Input Format:
One line: comma-separated tags with no spaces

Output Format:
One tag per line, in order.

Constraints:
1 <= tags <= 10, each tag 1..20 chars, no spaces
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= tags <= 10, each tag 1..20 chars, no spaces
questions.sourcecode:
line = input()
tags = line.split(",")
for t in tags:
    print(t)

questions.title: Label Half Splitter
questions.description:
A factory label printer splits product codes in half to stamp them on two sides.
Read a word of even length, print its first half, then its second half.

Input Format:
One line: a word of even length (lowercase letters)

Output Format:
Line 1: first half. Line 2: second half.

Constraints:
2 <= len(word) <= 100, even length, lowercase letters
questions.sourcecode:
word = input()
n = len(word) // 2
print(word[:n])
print(word[n:])

questions.title: Marquee Letters One Per Line
questions.description:
A theatre marquee controller receives words as character streams.
Read a word and print each character on its own line, in order, by iterating over the string.

Input Format:
One line: a word

Output Format:
One character per line.

Constraints:
1 <= len(word) <= 40

questions.title: Cinema Snack Receipt Line
questions.description:
A cinema kiosk prints one receipt line per snack order.
Read the snack name and its price, then print the receipt line with the money value formatted to exactly 2 decimals using an f-string.

Input Format:
Line 1: the snack name (letters and spaces)
Line 2: the price (a number)

Output Format:

Constraints:

questions.title: Airline Code Normalizer
questions.description:
At an airline check-in desk, passengers scribble airport codes with stray spaces and random capitalization.
Read the raw code, strip the surrounding whitespace, and print it in uppercase.

Input Format:
One line: the raw airport code, possibly padded with spaces, any case

Output Format:
The normalized code: trimmed and fully uppercase.

Constraints:
The code has exactly 3 letters, possibly padded with spaces on either side

questions.title: Club Username Generator
questions.description:
A gaming club auto-generates usernames: the first 3 letters of the member's display name joined with the last 2 digits of their phone number.
Build the username using slicing and concatenation.

Input Format:
Line 1: display name (letters, length 3..20)
Line 2: phone number (exactly 10 digits)

Output Format:
The generated username.

Constraints:
3 <= len(name) <= 20, phone has exactly 10 digits

questions.title: Masked Card Number
questions.description:
A payment page masks saved cards: it shows the first 4 digits and the last 4 digits, and replaces the middle 8 digits with '*' characters.
Rebuild the masked number using slicing and concatenation.

Input Format:
One line: the 16-digit card number

Output Format:
The masked card: first 4 digits, then one '*' per masked digit, then the last 4 digits.

Constraints:
Exactly 16 digits

questions.title: E-Invoice Grand Total
questions.description:
A billing clerk totals an e-invoice by hand because the fancy printer module is down.
Read n items (name and price each), add up the prices, and print the total amount formatted to exactly 2 decimals using str.format ONLY - f-strings are not allowed on this terminal.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of items
Next n lines: item_name price (the name is a single word)

Output Format:
Print exactly: Total: <sum with exactly 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= price <= 10000, item names have no spaces
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= price <= 10000, names have no spaces
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
total = 0.0
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split()
    total += float(parts[1])
print('Total: ' + '{:.2f}'.format(total))

questions.title: Teleprompter Word Reversal
questions.description:
A radio jockey's teleprompter stores lines word-by-word backwards for a tongue-twister segment.
Read the sentence and print it with the word order reversed, keeping single spaces between words. Reverse the word order with a manual loop - no slicing tricks.

Input Format:
One line: words separated by single spaces (lowercase letters)

Output Format:
The same words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= words <= 50, each word 1..20 lowercase letters
questions.input2: a b c d e f
questions.output2: f e d c b a
questions.sourcecode:
line = input()
words = line.split()
out = []
for i in range(len(words) - 1, -1, -1):
    out.append(words[i])
print(" ".join(out))

questions.title: Vault Codeword Palindrome
questions.description:
A security vault only opens when the day's codeword reads the same forwards and backwards.
Check the codeword manually with a two-pointer loop (compare the first and last characters while moving inward) - no slicing shortcuts.

Input Format:
One line: the codeword (lowercase letters)

Output Format:
Print "Palindrome" if it reads the same both ways, otherwise "Not Palindrome".

Constraints:
1 <= len(word) <= 100, lowercase letters only
questions.sourcecode:
word = input()
left = 0
right = len(word) - 1
is_pal = True
while left < right:
    if word[left] != word[right]:
        is_pal = False
        break
    left += 1
    right -= 1
if is_pal:
    print("Palindrome")
else:
    print("Not Palindrome")

questions.title: Chat Censor Filter
questions.description:
A chat moderation bot masks banned words instead of deleting them: every standalone occurrence of the banned word is replaced by asterisks of the same length.
Words are separated by single spaces and contain no punctuation. A word is masked only when it exactly equals the banned word (so "robot" survives when the banned word is "bot").

Input Format:
Line 1: the banned word (lowercase letters)
Line 2: the message (lowercase words separated by single spaces)

Output Format:
The censored message with each banned word replaced by '*' repeated for its length.

Constraints:
1 <= len(banned) <= 15, 1 <= words <= 30, lowercase letters only
questions.sampleinput1:
spam
this spam message is spam

questions.title: Triage Name Tag Formatter
questions.description:
A hospital triage desk prints name tags where every word of the patient's name starts with a capital letter and the rest is lowercase.
The label printer firmware blocks .title() and .capitalize(), so build each word manually: uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest.

Input Format:
One line: the full name, words separated by single spaces (letters only, any case)

Output Format:
The normalized name on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= words <= 8, each word 1..20 letters
questions.sourcecode:
line = input()
words = line.split()
out = []
for w in words:
    out.append(w[0].upper() + w[1:].lower())
print(" ".join(out))

questions.title: Greenhouse Sensor Board
questions.description:
A greenhouse dashboard prints sensor readings in fixed-width columns: the sensor name left-aligned in a width-10 column, the reading right-aligned in a width-6 column with exactly 2 decimals.
Use f-string format specifiers for the alignment.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of sensors
Next n lines: sensor_name reading (the name is a single word; the reading is a number)

Output Format:
n lines, each: the name left-aligned in width 10, then the reading right-aligned in width 6 with 2 decimals.

questions.title: Staff Roster Beautifier
questions.description:
An HR intern pastes raw comma-separated staff records into a report tool that formats valid rows into aligned columns and rejects broken rows.
Each record line is name,dept,score. A record is valid only when it splits into exactly 3 fields, name and dept are non-empty, and score is a digit string whose value is at most 100. Valid records print as aligned rows; anything else prints INVALID.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of records
Next n lines: name,dept,score (fields contain no spaces)

Output Format:
For each valid record print: name left-aligned in width 10, dept left-aligned in width 12, score right-aligned in width 3.
For each invalid record print: INVALID
Finally print: Valid records: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, fields 0..15 chars without spaces, score is a digit string
questions.sampleoutput1:
ramesh    sales        88
INVALID
priya     eng          95
Valid records: 2
questions.output2:
vikram    it           77
INVALID
ana       ops           7
INVALID
Valid records: 2
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, fields 0..15 chars without spaces, score is a digit string
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
valid_count = 0
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split(",")
    ok = False
    name = ""
    dept = ""
    score = ""
    if len(parts) == 3:
        name, dept, score = parts
        if name != "" and dept != "" and score.isdigit() and int(score) <= 100:
            ok = True
    if ok:
        valid_count += 1
        print(f"{name:<10}{dept:<12}{score:>3}")
    else:
        print("INVALID")
print(f"Valid records: {valid_count}")

questions.title: Certificate Template Engine
questions.description:
An academy's certificate generator fills placeholder tokens written as {key} inside a template line.
The string-method toolbox on the print server is broken, so fill the template by scanning it character by character: when a { starts a token, read until } and substitute the mapped value.
Every token in the template has a mapping.

Input Format:
Line 1: the template line (may contain {key} placeholders)
Line 2: n, the number of mappings
Next n lines: key value (the value is a single token without spaces)

Output Format:
The filled template line.

Constraints:
1 <= len(template) <= 300, 1 <= n <= 10, tokens are well-formed {key} with no nesting
questions.sampleinput1:
Dear {student}, welcome to {course}. Grade: {grade}.
3
student Meera
course PyBasics
grade A
questions.sampleoutput1: Dear Meera, welcome to PyBasics. Grade: A.
questions.input2:
Order {id} total {amount} INR
2
id A-1029
amount 4500
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(template) <= 300, 1 <= n <= 10, values have no spaces
questions.sourcecode:
template = input()
n = int(input())
values = {}
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split()
    values[parts[0]] = parts[1]
out = []
i = 0
while i < len(template):
    ch = template[i]
    if ch == "{":
        j = template.find("}", i)
        key = template[i + 1:j]
        out.append(values[key])
        i = j + 1
    else:
        out.append(ch)
        i += 1
print("".join(out))
